title: Added depth control for consistent character generation
author: Kaninen_Ka9en
selftext: We recently added depth control for consistent character generation in [Pixellab](http://www.pixellab.ai). You can create an account and try it out for free on our website :) Use the tool "Image to image (depth)"

replies.author: Synyster328
replies.body:
It's a generative AI/Diffusion model term. Creates a "depth map", sort of a grayscale version of an image where darker is further away, lighter is closer. Then then generation model uses that as guidance to generate any sort of image that mostly adheres to the same depths.

It keeps things with mostly the same structure while having totally different textures or colors

comments.author: EmergentTurtleHead
comments.body:
For anyone considering paying for this product:

1. Go to ChatGPT. Ask it to generate an image of the character you are imagining. Include a reference image if you want. In your prompt include something like "real pixel art, uniform pixels perfectly aligned to a pixel grid, 16bit SNES".
2. Regenerate until you are happy. Download the image and open it in your editor of choice. I use Gimp.
3. Turn on the grid. Adjust it to fit the general size of the pixels in your image, and shift it horizontall/vertically until the pixels generally line up. The AI art won't be perfect but you should be able to get it close.
4. Crop the image so that it only contains whole grid squares, cutting out the incomplete squares around the edge.
5. Resize the image with interpolation disabled, to dimensions equal to the image dimension divided by the grid square size. You now have "real" pixel art with no blurry or malformed pixels. Congrats!
